headline: Profit jumps on broad growth as buybacks continue
summary_short: Wells Fargo's Q2 2026 net income rose 17% y/y (22% q/q) to $6,407M on 9% y/y revenue growth to $22,622M, with diluted EPS up 25% y/y to $2.00, helped by a $132M discrete tax benefit and continued share buybacks.
summary_long: Revenue rose 9% y/y to $22,622M as net interest income grew 5% on lower deposit costs and balance-sheet growth while noninterest income rose 13% on venture-capital gains and higher advisory/investment-banking fees. Net income climbed 17% y/y (22% q/q) to $6,407M, aided by expense discipline (efficiency ratio improved to 60% from 64%) and a $132M discrete tax benefit. Diluted EPS rose 25% y/y to $2.00. Credit quality stayed strong: net charge-offs fell 11% y/y and provision for credit losses declined 9%. Wells Fargo repurchased $3.0B of stock in the quarter and expects to raise its Q3 dividend 11% to $0.50/share, up from $0.45. CET1 ratio was 10.3%, down from 11.1% a year ago.

drivers.explanation: Net interest income rose 5% on lower deposit costs and balance-sheet growth; noninterest income rose 13% on venture-capital gains and higher advisory/investment-banking fees.
Broad-based revenue growth and expense discipline (efficiency ratio improved to 60%) drove profit higher, plus a $132M discrete tax benefit from resolving prior-period tax matters.
EPS grew faster than net income (25% vs 17% y/y) because diluted shares outstanding fell 5.9% y/y on continued buybacks, adding extra per-share lift.
Pretax income rose as provision for credit losses fell 9% y/y on strong consumer and commercial credit quality, letting revenue growth flow through to pretax profit.
CEO Scharf cited EPS growth of 25% y/y, positive operating leverage, strong credit quality, and 12% y/y average loan growth as broad-based momentum across all four operating segments.
